text: dsh-honcho 是为 DSH CLI 提供 Honcho 长期记忆的插件。它在 agent 回合前获取用户档案、会话摘要和相关结论，并注入提示词；首回合等待有五秒上限，之后后台刷新。插件也会捕获、脱敏并上传用户与助手消息，提供历史搜索、记忆问答和保存记忆三个工具，以及 /honcho 状态、配置查看和立即同步命令。适合希望跨会话保留偏好、项目背景和决策的 DSH 用户，需要 Honcho API key。

dsh-honcho gives the DSH CLI persistent Honcho memory. It injects profiles and relevant session context, captures and uploads redacted conversations, and offers tools to search, ask about, and save memories. Use /honcho to view status or sync. Requires a Honcho API key.
想让 DSH 记住我以前说过的偏好和项目背景。
有没有办法把 Honcho 里的个人记忆自动带进每次 DSH 对话？
我希望不同会话还能接着用之前记录的长期信息。
帮 DSH 在会话结束后保存用户和助手的对话内容。
能不能在 DSH 里搜索我以前聊过的内容和总结？
我想把重要决定保存起来，下次开新会话还能查到。
How can I give my coding assistant persistent memory across sessions?
I want to search past conversations and save durable preferences from DSH.
Can my assistant automatically load relevant user context before a turn?
How do I manually sync captured conversations to Honcho?
dsh-honcho 的功能「注入记忆」：回合前获取摘要、用户档案和相关结论并作为提示词上下文；首次等待最多五秒，之后后台刷新。
dsh-honcho 的功能「捕获并同步会话消息」：从 DSH 持久事件日志选取用户与助手消息，按会话游标切片后上传；在回合边界、压缩前或退出时刷新。
dsh-honcho 的功能「搜索历史记忆」：honcho_search 并行搜索原始消息和派生结论，合并后返回文本。
dsh-honcho 的功能「询问用户偏好」：honcho_chat 将问题交给 Honcho 推理，可关联当前会话并使用配置的观察视角。
dsh-honcho 的功能「保存长期记忆」：honcho_remember 将非空内容保存为关于用户的持久结论，并关联当前 Honcho 会话。
dsh-honcho 的功能「查看状态与配置」：/honcho 显示 peer、workspace、session、捕获与注入状态及 dashboard 链接；/honcho config 显示解析后的配置。
dsh-honcho 的功能「立即刷新消息」：/honcho flush 调用 flushAll，同步尚未上传的会话事件并返回结果。
dsh-honcho 会将捕获的用户与助手消息发送到 Honcho；上传前会对常见凭据格式和自定义 noisePatterns 做正则脱敏。
使用前需要 Honcho API key；插件默认连接 api.honcho.dev，也可通过配置修改 baseUrl 连接自托管服务。

[Honcho](https://honcho.dev).

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · dsh-honcho：`dsh` forgets everything when a session ends. This plugin gives it memory that doesn't: what you're building,
how you like to work, what you decided last week and why. It reads the same `~/.honcho/config.json` as the
other Honcho integrations, so there is one place to configure all of them — and pointing two of them at the
same `workspace` gives them one shared memory.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add @honcho-ai/dsh-honcho
```

Then put your API key and name in `~/.honcho/config.json`:

```json
{
  "peerName": "your-name",
  "auth": { "apiKey": "${HONCHO_API_KEY}" },
  "hosts": {

Get a key at [app.honcho.dev](https://app.honcho.dev). `HONCHO_API_KEY` in the environment also works on its
own — the config file is only needed to change defaults.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · What it does：**Captures every turn.** User and assistant messages go to Honcho in the background, debounced, and flushed at
turn boundaries, before compaction, and on shutdown. Common secret formats are redacted first (API keys and
tokens, `password:`/`secret:` fields, private keys, JWTs, cookies, connection strings, credential URLs). This is
regex matching, so it is best-effort: an unusual format, or a bare high-entropy string with no label, can still
get through. Add your own with `capture.noisePatterns`, or turn capture off with `capture.saveMessages`.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · What it does：| Tool              | For                                                                        |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `honcho_search`   | Looking something up. Searches raw messages _and_ derived conclusions.     |
| `honcho_chat`     | Asking a question of judgment. Reasons over everything Honcho knows. Slow. |
| `honcho_remember` | Saving a durable fact, preference, or decision.                            |
@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · What it does：**`/honcho`** shows status and a link to the session in the Honcho dashboard — see Commands below.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Configuration：Everything behavioral lives in `~/.honcho/config.json` under `hosts.dsh` — the same file `claude-honcho`,
`codex-honcho`, and the other integrations read. Root holds identity and connection; the host block holds
behavior.

The file is read as strict JSON: the comments and trailing commas below are annotation only. Leave them in and
the whole file is skipped without a warning, so every setting falls back to its default.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Injection components：The two menus differ in **cadence**, not in what they can carry.

`injection.sessionStart` is injected once when a session opens: `directives` (guidance on using memory),
`summary`, `peerCard`, `representation`.

`injection.perTurn` refreshes as you work:

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Injection components：- **`userContext`** — a fresh, prompt-scoped peer context blob: **representation + peer card**, retrieved using
  your current message as the search query so recall is associative rather than merely recent. It is a bundle,
  so it supplies both regardless of what `sessionStart` names. To get one without the other, name it in
  `sessionStart` and set `perTurn: []` — at the cost of per-turn refresh.
- **`dialectic`** — a reasoned answer about you, run every `cadence.dialectic` turns and shaped by
  `injection.dialectic`. Nothing waits on it after the first turn, so a late answer reaches the next one.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Injection components：Components the canonical schema names but this plugin does not implement — `briefing`, `assistantContext`,
`sessionContext` — are reported at startup rather than silently dropped, as are schema keys it does not act on
(`showContents`, `statusline`, `globalOverride`, granular `observation`, `multiUser`) and any key renamed since
an earlier version. Nothing here is accepted and quietly ignored.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Injection components：The plugin's own `cordis.yml` config carries plumbing only — `configPath`, `apiKeyRef`, `host`, `enabled`. Set
`host` to run a credential-isolated profile (`"dsh_work"`) against the same install.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Sessions：Default: one long-lived session per project directory, named `<peerName>-<dir>`, matching claude-honcho. Pin a
different name for any path with the root `sessions` map — an override always wins.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Sessions：| `sessionStrategy`         | Session name            | Notes                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `per-directory` (default) | `<peer>-<dir>`          | Stable across restarts and branches                                |
| `per-repo`                | `<peer>-<repo-root>`    | Same memory from any subdirectory                                  |
| `git-remote`              | `<peer>-<host-owner-repo>` | From the `origin` URL, so the same repo on two machines is one session. Falls back to `per-directory` outside a repo or without an `origin` |
| `git-branch`              | `<peer>-<dir>-<branch>` | Falls back to `per-directory` outside a repo or on a detached HEAD |
| `per-session`             | `<peer>-chat-<id>`      | A clean slate every restart                                        |
| `global`                  | `<peer>`                | One memory for everything                                          |

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Sessions：`per-directory` and `per-repo` name a session after a folder, so two different projects that both live in a
`web` directory silently share one memory across machines. `git-remote` is the fix: it reduces the `origin` URL
to `host/owner/repo`, so `git@github.com:you/web.git` and `https://github.com/you/web` agree, and `you/web` and
`someone-else/web` do not. It compares the URL as configured, so machines that clone through different ssh
`Host` aliases — `github.com-work` on one, `github.com` on the other — still get separate sessions.

@honcho-ai/dsh-honcho README · Commands：| Command          | Does                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/honcho`        | Status: peer, workspace, session, strategy, pending uploads, last sync, last fetch |
| `/honcho config` | Resolved settings, the file they came from, and any ignored injection components   |
| `/honcho flush`  | Sync now                                                                           |
